name: Powkiddy X55
summary: Powkiddy's 5.5-inch RK3566-based Android/Linux handheld with a 1280×720 landscape IPS display. Boots open-source Linux from SD; stock card is the whole system, so a replacement OS is a card swap and going back to stock is a card write.
openByDesign: KNULLI and ROCKNIX boot from an SD card with no unlock or patch

specs.cpu: Rockchip RK3566 Quad-core ARM Cortex-A55, 1.8 GHz
specs.storage: 16 GB built-in; TF card expansion up to 256 GB

variants.storage: 16 GB built-in, TF up to 256 GB
variants.notes: Large 5.5-inch landscape IPS display at 1280×720. RK3566 with 1 GB LPDDR4X RAM. TF card support up to 256 GB. Battery life claimed 4 hours, 2 h charge. Supports HDMI video output via USB-C. Console weight 293 g, dimensions 212.5×94.5×19 mm.

specs.storage: 16 GB built-in, TF up to 256 GB
specs.interfaces: USB-C fast charging, HDMI display via OTG, 3.5 mm stereo jack

firmware.version: Open source Linux (stock); Jelos system variant exists

homebrew.name: KNULLI
homebrew.firmware: Per-model image (knulli-rk3568-powkiddy-x55); boots from SD card with no stock-firmware dependency.
homebrew.summary: Batocera-based retro gaming OS for the Powkiddy X55. Boots from a prepared SD card.

compatibility.note: KNULLI publishes an RK3566 image for the X55 with Rockchip BSP 4.19 and Mali GL driver.

requirements: A computer with an SD card reader and an image writer.
warnings: KNULLI ships a separate image per model; cross-flashing does not boot.

homebrew.name: ROCKNIX
homebrew.firmware: Per-model RK3566 image; boots from SD card.
homebrew.summary: Mainline-Linux retro gaming OS for the Powkiddy X55. Boots from SD card.

compatibility.note: ROCKNIX lists the X55 as a supported RK3566 device.

requirements: A computer with an SD card reader and an image writer.
warnings: ROCKNIX ships a separate image per model; cross-flashing does not boot.

homebrew.name: Powkiddy stock firmware
homebrew.firmware: Open source Linux on TF card; restore by writing the stock image.
homebrew.summary: Powkiddy's own Linux OS image on the TF card. Restoring the stock card restores the factory system.

compatibility.note: The stock OS lives on the TF card.

requirements: The stock TF card or a freshly flashed one from Powkiddy.
warnings: Remove any third-party OS card before booting stock.
